transcript.content: Hi, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um, yeah… thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because something at work got a little out of hand. I work in HR, and I was leading an onboarding launch, and I… pushed it forward before all the approvals were officially in place.

At the time it honestly felt like the right thing to do—decisive, necessary, like I was helping move things along. But I committed company money and vendor time, and now I’m on leave, and people are asking what I was thinking. So… I thought I should come talk to someone, if that makes sense.
Around the time you pushed the project forward, did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy compared with your normal self?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, but for the past few weeks I did feel kind of… unusually alive, I guess. Like I finally had the clarity and drive to show leadership what HR could really be.

And then, if someone questioned me—even over small things, like edits or routine budget questions—I could get suddenly really angry. More than I probably should have. At the time it felt justified, but looking back… yeah, it was not quite my usual self. Does that make sense?
During these past few weeks, have you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt energetic?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, my sleep has been a little uneven, but I don’t know that I’d say I needed much less and was fine, exactly. I wasn’t really tracking it closely.

I guess I was busy and keyed up with work, but… I don’t want to overstate it. What would count as “much less” in this context?
During this period, were there nights when you slept only a few hours and still felt fully rested the next day?

Maybe a few short nights, but I honestly don’t remember clearly enough to say, “yes, definitely.” I wasn’t keeping track, and I’d hate to give you the wrong answer.

I know I was staying up later thinking about work, but whether I only slept a couple hours and felt fully rested the next day… I’m not sure. Maybe there were times I pushed through and felt okay, but I don’t want to overstate it.
During that period, were you talking more than usual or feeling like you couldn't stop talking?

I guess… yes, probably more than usual. I don’t want to make it sound like I was out of control, but in meetings I’d catch myself talking faster and going on longer than I normally would.

Like I’d start on employee engagement, then somehow be talking about gallery layouts and retention metrics all in one stretch, and people would have to sort of… raise their hands or jump in to stop me. I thought I was being thorough at the time, but maybe it came across as a lot. Does that answer what you mean?
During that time, did you feel more powerful, important, or unusually confident than you normally do?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say “powerful,” exactly. That sounds a little dramatic to me.

I may have felt more confident than usual in some conversations, like I had good ideas and wanted people to see where I was going with them, but I’m not sure it crossed into feeling unusually important. Maybe I’m downplaying it a bit, but I didn’t think of it that way at the time. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
During that period, were you taking on a lot more projects or activities than you normally would?

Yeah… I think I probably was. I mean, at the time it felt like I was just being productive and trying to solve things, not like I was doing something unreasonable.

But I was trying to run the HR redesign, and then also line up gallery partners, reach out to festival organizers, and deal with several staff conflicts all kind of at the same time. And I remember feeling like if an idea came up, I had to move on it right away, before it got lost.

I don’t know if that counts as “a lot more” than normal, but looking back, it was probably more than I’d usually take on at once.
Because of this period, were you placed on leave from work or otherwise unable to function normally?

Um… yes. I mean, I’m technically on administrative leave right now.

I’d like to think it was more because things got complicated around the launch and some staff conflicts, not that I just couldn’t do my job, but… the way I handled it seems to have shaken people’s confidence in me. I’m not really trusted to manage the HR projects I was leading anymore.

That’s hard to say out loud, but yes, it did affect work in a pretty concrete way.
During that period, did you have experiences like hearing voices or strongly believing something that other people said wasn’t true?

No, I don’t think so. I wasn’t hearing voices or seeing things, if that’s what you mean.

As far as believing things other people said weren’t true… I mean, people disagreed with me, definitely, but I don’t think I was convinced of something unreal. I felt strongly about my ideas, maybe too strongly, but not like… out of touch with reality. At least I don’t think so. Does that answer it?
Before this recent period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually energized or activated like this for several days or more?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had busy stretches before, definitely, where I was really engaged with work or kind of running on momentum for a few days. But I don’t know that I would’ve called it unusual at the time.

Nothing is coming to mind that feels exactly like this recent period. Maybe I’m not thinking about it the right way, though. What would count as “activated” in the way you mean?
Before this recent period, was there ever another time in your life when you felt unusually energized and not like your usual self for several days in a row?

I don’t think so… not in a way I can clearly point to.

I’ve had times where I was busy or maybe more upbeat than usual, but several days in a row where I felt really not like myself—before this recent thing—I’m not aware of that. If it happened, I didn’t recognize it that way at the time. Does that make sense?
Before this recent period, had there ever been another time in your life when you felt unusually high, irritable, or full of energy for several days in a row?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve probably had normal ups and downs—stressful weeks, times I was more motivated or more on edge—but before this recent period, I can’t really think of another stretch of several days where I was unusually high or energized like that.

I hope that’s clear. I’m trying not to overstate it either way.
